issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method named checkOrderReady() to be implemented and called from orderMeal() to process orders. The solution implementation uses a differently named method processOrders() (and orderMeal() calls processOrders()). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about the required method name and expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name with the specification: either rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady() in the solution (and ensure orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady()), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to processOrders(). Preferably provide a checkOrderReady() public method (which may delegate to an internal helper) so students clearly see and implement the required API.

issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a method named checkOrderReady() to attempt serving queued orders. In the reference solution the same behavior is implemented in a method named processOrders(), and there is no checkOrderReady() method. This naming difference (checkOrderReady vs. processOrders) refers to the same conceptual operation (serve ready orders) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students implementing the required API and when they compare their implementation to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent method name for the order-serving operation across problem text, template, and solution. Either (A) rename processOrders() in the solution to checkOrderReady() and update any internal calls accordingly, or (B) add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(), and update the problem statement to mention the delegated name if needed. This preserves the intended behavior while aligning identifiers.
